articleTitle: Wide-band Kriging based Optimization for EMC of a Half Bridge Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: With the increasing complexity of electronic systems and their miniaturization, Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) concerns have increased due to the higher switching frequencies of buck/boost power converters. Electromagnetic Interference filters are used to comply with EMC limits. However, the optimal to-the-limit design of such a power system is difficult due to the large number of involved parameters which, in case of complex EMC simulation models, lead to prohibitively long simulation times. This paper develops a method based on wide-band surrogate models of a half bridge buck converter and its EMI filter, which is fast enough to allow 10,000 system evaluations in 4 minutes with an octa-core laptop. With the surrogate models, we demonstrate the feasibility of Multi-Objective Optimization (MOO) for minimizing common-mode emission and the size of the filter’s common-mode choke. A computational advantage over LTspice simulations of at least 400 times has been achieved.

articleTitle: Mode-decomposition-based Equivalent Via (MEV) Model and MEV Model Application Range Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: The mode-decomposition-based equivalent via (MEV) model is proposed in this paper, which is a physics-based equivalent model for the high-speed channel modeling. The application ranges of the MEV model are analyzed by varying anti-pad radius, via radius, and distance between the parallel plates for a single via with multiple layers. Based on the S-parameter comparison with full-wave simulations, the MEV model is useful for the insertion loss calculation up to 100 GHz. Meanwhile, the return loss from the MEV model shows a high level of correlation with full-wave simulation results up to 70GHz, even when the anti-pad radius is larger than the commonly used size. The parallel-plate height has a negligible impact on the accuracy of the MEV model. This paper demonstrates the large application range of the MEV model and verifies that MEV model is suitable for practical high-speed via analysis.

articleTitle: Research on Simulation of Conductive Immunity of IO Control Module of Digital Control Circuit Based on ARM
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: This paper firstly analyzes the research status of integrated circuit (IC) electromagnetic and digital control circuit electromagnetic immunity simulation. Secondly, the parameters of passive devices on the coupling path of direct power injection interference of a set of digital control circuits based on ARM are extracted and the equivalent circuit model is established, and the IO pin simulation calculation model based on direct interference injection is established. The transient interference signal and continuous wave signal are used as interference input respectively, and the port response of ARM chip under the two kinds of interference is simulated.

articleTitle: Crosstalk Reduction in Coupled Microstrip Lines using TT-shaped DMS Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: The electromagnetic coupling between closely placed microstrip lines in compact and dense designs causes crosstalk which is undesired and hence should be minimized. In this context, several approaches have been evaluated in the literature, including via fencing, guard trace, guard trace with via, serpentine guard trace, serpentine guard trace with vias, serpentine microstrip lines, asymmetrically loaded microstrip lines, etc.; however, these structures require additional space between microstrip lines. Besides, some defective microstrip line structures (DMS) are proposed, which are difficult to fabricate, possess limited crosstalk improvement, and lag the rigorous DMS parametric analyses. Therefore in this regard, we propose a DMS approach consisting of arrays of the combinations of T and inverted T, etched on one of the coupled microstrip lines (CMLs), which alters the current path in the etched microstrip line, and this, in turn, reduces the coupling and hence reduces the crosstalk. In addition to the above, rigorous parametric analyses have also been performed, allowing the designer to tune the length of the structure to minimize the crosstalk at the desired frequency. Furthermore, the simulations of the TT-shaped DMS, performed on a 75x50mm RO4003 rogers PCB in the frequency range of 1-10GHz, show a minimum improvement of 12dB and a maximum improvement of 62dB, which outperforms the existing DMSs.

articleTitle: Analysis of Voltage Regulator Module (VRM) Noise Coupling to High-Speed Signals with VRM Via Designs
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: The physical noise coupling mechanism between voltage regulator module (VRM) noise coupling to high-speed signal traces is analyzed and different noise reduction methods are analyzed for the first time. The rapid switching of field effect transistors (FETs) creates an unintentional coupling region around the VRM. As high-speed traces are often routed in the inner signal layers of printed circuit boards (PCBs) as striplines for signal integrity, the VRM switching noise is mainly coupled from noisy power vias to the victim traces routed around the VRM region. To analyze different coupling reduction methods in practical high-speed channels, a simplified PCB design based on a high-speed server platform is proposed. Case studies under various conditions verifies the most effective VRM noise coupling reduction method. Different design parameters that influence the VRM noise coupling are analyzed to provide a design guide for high-speed channel designers.

articleTitle: Enhanced Signal and Power Integrity using Novel Planar EBG design
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Simultaneous switching noise (SSN), often occurs when signals transition rapidly between the ground and power planes, is an important problem in high-speed digital circuits. The Electromagnetic Bandgap Structure (EBG) is a novel technique that can help to solve signal integrity and power integrity problems. In this paper, we present a three dimensional coplanar electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure to improve Signal Integrity (SI) , validated by eye diagram and Power Integrity (PI) shown by self impedance. This proposed planar EBG structure offers effective SSN suppression for frequency ranges between 2.38 GHz and 22.39 GHz, with an average suppression level of -30 dB.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of Characteristic Mode Analysis (CMA) using Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: In this work, a novel experimental validation of characteristic mode analysis (CMA) is proposed using reverberation chamber measurements. Using the modal weighting coefficient formulation based on the magnetic moment and modal H field obtained from solvers, the total radiated power (TRP) is calculated. This TRP is compared with the TRP obtained from the reverberation chamber measurements. A good correlation between the simulation and measurement was achieved for a simple rectangular plate of size 15 cm × 8 cm with an error of less than 4 dB.

articleTitle: Dual Stop Band and Narrow Pass Band FSS Structure for Shielding Sub-6 GHz 5G Band Signals and Reduce EMI to Radio Altimeter
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient approach is proposed to achieve shielding of sub-6 GHz 5G band n77 (3.3-4.2 GHz), n78 (3.3-3.8 GHz), and n79 (4.4-5 GHz) signals to prevent interference with radio altimeters operations (4.2-4.4 GHz) in Aeronautical Radio-Navigational Services (ARNS) band. In this paper two designs are proposed, one on a low-cost FR4 substrate and the other on a low loss Taconic TLY-5 substrate. The proposed FSS structure on TLY-5 substrate offers a narrow pass band response at 4.3 GHz with a 200 MHz bandwidth (BW) and an insertion loss (IL) of -0.5 dB for satisfactory radio altimeter operations (4.2-4.4 GHz), along with band stop response at 3.74 GHz with 50 dB shielding and at 4.53 GHz with 39.5 dB shielding. The FSS structure on FR4 substrate offers a narrow pass band response at 4.3 GHz with -3 dB insertion loss (IL) along with a band stop response at 3.74 GHz with 31.5 dB shielding and at 4.62 GHz with 24.5 dB shielding. The proposed FSS unit cell contains a square loop patch with 8 axe arms attached to it. This unit cell design is printed on 0.8mm substrate thickness. The proposed FSS structure is symmetrical and provides a stable angular response up to 60° of incidence for both the transverse electric (TE) mode and the transverse magnetic (TM) mode. To validate the design, a prototype of the proposed FSS structure is fabricated on FR4 Substrate and its results obtained were compared with simulation results. Both simulated and measured results were in congruence with each other.

articleTitle: Simulation Modeling for Radiated Emission of USB Cable Enabling Shielding Impact Investigations
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: The excessive radiation emission (RE) from universal series bus (USB) cable has raised great concerns with the fast increase of data transmission speed. In this paper, a simulation model combining both full-wave and transmission line solver has been developed to predict RE from a typical USB 2.0 system in data-transmission mode. The simulation model enables investigations on the impact of different cable parameters on its RE, the conclusion offers guidelines for USB cable design in terms of RE reduction from the source.

articleTitle: Application of TVS Models for SEED Simulation of a Variety of TVS Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Accurate models of transient voltage suppression (TVS) devices are important for determining the suitability of electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection strategies early in the design process. An improved TVS model is used in the following paper to represent a variety of TVS devices, including a snapback device, non-snapback device, and a varistor. The models include recent improvements to represent conductivity modulation and the overall shape of the TVS device’s transient response. The models are tuned based on characterizations of these protection devices using a transmission line pulse (TLP), and are then used in a system efficient ESD design (SEED) simulation to predict the transient voltages and currents in a system consisting of an off-chip TVS, an IC with on-chip ESD protection, and a PCB trace in between. Simulated transient voltage and current waveforms closely match measurements both when testing the TVS devices by themselves and in SEED simulations. Peak and quasistatic currents through the TVS and on-chip diode were typically captured within about 10% or less across the devices tested while varying both the rise time and level of the injected TLP.

articleTitle: EMC and protection of 1 MW klystron RF system for proton accelerator
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: For low energy high intensity proton accelerator (LEHIPA), Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) has developed the three of 352 MHz, 1 MW klystron based high power radio frequency (RF) systems to power three accelerating cavities. The 1 MW RF system comprises of interlock and protection system, low voltage (LV) and high voltage (HV) bias supplies, harmonic filter, directional coupler, circulator, wave guide window, RF load and WR2300 wave guide components. Fasting acting Interlock and Protection system (IPS) is used for safe and reliable operation of high power RF system. This 1 MW klystron based high power RF system (inclusive of HV DC supplies) generates the high RF power and may generate RF interference (RFI) in the form of conducted emission and radiated emission.All the bias supplies of the RF system are controlled by IPS, which have to function satisfactory in RFI environment. Hence, Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of IPS and other sub systems must be required. So EM suppression techniques and practices have been designed, developed and successfully implemented within klystron RF system, which has been integrated to accelerator.This paper, discusses the details of klystron RF system and electromagnetic compatibility achieved and tested by addressing most of the issues by quieting the sources of interference, inhibiting coupling paths and hardening the potential victims.

articleTitle: Design strategies for Signal Integrity, Power Integrity and EMI EMC issues in Computing boards and Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: In the modern world, complexity of electronic products has increased due to the demand for higher performance such as faster data transfers, better image processing, higher computing power, and greater functionality. The technological advancements towards multi-core CPU and GPGPU environments in a single Printed Circuit Board has brought up various design challenges and constraints for compute and signal processing systems. One such challenge is to meet the Signal, Power Integrity and stringent EMI/EMC standards for the equipment based on the installation platform. The operating frequencies of processor clocks and switching frequencies of interfaces are ranging from few MHz to 10 GHz. The improper terminations of the high-speed signals not only affect the system performance but also its surrounding system performance through emissions. Hence it is very much essential to sensitize on various challenges involved in Signal, Power Integrity, EMI EMC qualification of a high-end Computing and Signal Processing system.

articleTitle: EMC Design for a Ship Borne Real Time Embedded System
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Most real time embedded hardware systems are made to operate under harsh electromagnetic interference (EMI) conditions. The problem is more severe if the system is operating in a marine environment where it co-exists with several simultaneous sources of emission such as communication equipments, auxiliary antennas, Satellite Communication (SATCOM) links etc used in the ship. Therefore, it is imperative that the system must be resilient to the EMI happening in the environment, and at the same time it should not be a source of EMI for other systems operating in its vicinity. One way to ensure this is to design the system with adequate diligence so that the system passes the Conducted Emission (CE), Radiated Emission (RE), Conducted Susceptibility (CS) and Radiated Susceptibility (RS) Tests as specified in MIL-STD-461G. We present in this paper a case study for the design of such a real time embedded system with proper Grounding, Shielding and Bonding Schemes implemented in the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) design. Additional features like Galvanic isolation in I/O Translation board is present for protection against transients. Improved protection by way of EMI gaskets, 360 degree shielding on the system cables, separation of isolated ground from chassis ground, separate shield for each Processing Board (PCB), using isolated power supply, usage of proper Transient Voltage Suppressor (TVS) diodes and EMI Filters, adequate number of ground pins on every connector, usage of differential RS-422 signals are the prominent features which has offered ruggedness to this system from EMI. The real time embedded hardware system has successfully passed the EMI EMC tests to which the unit was subjected.

articleTitle: DDR5 Electrical Challenges in High-Speed Server Design
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Memory technologies are constantly trying to keep-up pace with the ever-increasing demand for compute and bandwidth. In high-speed servers, the single-ended technology of double data rate (DDR) synchronous dynamic random-access memory (SDRAM) has evolved from its humble beginnings to its fifth generation in DDR5. DDR5 operating speed can range from 3200 Mbps to north of 6400 Mbps (~ 8000 Mbps). In servers, DDR5 is usually supported through dual in-line memory modules (DIMMs). As the DDR speeds continue to increase, the operating margins are shrinking to tens of millivolts and picoseconds. Any imperfection in the channel routing can adversely impact the signal integrity (SI) margins.In this paper, SI challenges related to operating a single-ended DDR5 interface at such high-speeds is discussed. Various test cases are used to demonstrate the numerous challenges. The scenarios covered in this paper include the effects of channel imperfections like reflections and crosstalk, the importance of optimal routing layer assignment, impact of multiple DIMMs in the channel and the value of receiver equalization.

articleTitle: A Method to Measure the Electromagnetic Emission Induced by Electromagnetic Interference of Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: In this paper, we present a method to characterize the electromagnetic emission (EME) of integrated circuits (ICs) caused by electromagnetic interference (EMI). Normally, emission and immunity of ICs are measured separately, but this does not correspond exactly to the application. In reality, an IC always experiences disturbances at its inputs. In order to better illustrate and understand the more realistic measurement of the emission behaviour of an IC, taking into account disturbances on its inputs, we introduce the ELectromagnetic InTerference and Emission (ELITE) plot. The ELITE plot is particularly useful for visually representing the EME caused by EMI, and provides a clear understanding of how the electromagnetic emission changes with the frequency of the interference signal. The method involves applying a disturbance signal in the frequency range 1MHz to 1GHz to one pin of the IC and measuring the EME simultaneously at another IC pin. We demonstrate the use of this method with a smart power high-side switch as an example. We also provide instructions for creating an ELITE plot from measurements using a measurement setup combining the direct power injection (DPI) and 150Ω method.

articleTitle: Half TEM horn Antenna for Compact Pulsed Transformer based UWB System
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Transverse Electromagnetic (TEM) horn antenna is very commonly used for radiating very short pulses with subnanosecond rise time. Compact pulse transformer based ultra wideband (UWB) system (120 kV, 150 ns) at BARC Vizag also uses a TEM Horn antenna of 100 Ohm input impedance. This is an unbalanced type of antenna which is having a half TEM horn with ground plane. Ground plane here is expanded gradually into a plane structure from outer conductor of coaxial structure in order to avoid sudden discontinuities. In this paper simulation results for TEM horn antenna are presented. Comparison of boresight electric fields is also done between simulated results and experimental results available.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Simulation-based Digital Front-Loading for Conducted Emission Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: The challenge for Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) and Compatibility (EMC) compliance is exponentially growing with the demand and growth of electric vehicles. Thus, digitally evaluating the EMI/EMC at the early design stages becomes vital. This paper highlights the analysis of multiple modules within a sub-system from a typical electric vehicle architecture. The measured conducted emissions of individual modules are compared to the simulated results yielded by two approaches; one based on the measurement of excitation waveforms and the other based on the modelling of the excitation waveforms. The comparison between the results summarizes the accuracy and limitations of the modelled approaches to attain high-fidelity digital front-loading methods.

articleTitle: Spacecraft charging analysis for Chandrayaan-2 mission
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: The interaction of a spacecraft with its orbital environment is a major consideration which must be addressed during the design of any space system, since a variety of hazards are associated with the operation of spacecraft in the harsh space environment. The Indian lunar mission Chanrayaan-2 spacecraft was expected to experience different plasma environmental conditions during its full mission life. These plasma environments include environment during earth centric phase, transfer to lunar orbit phase, lunar orbit phase & post landing phase. Out of all plasma environment conditions, earth bound phase is much more severe than any GEO mission as spacecraft is expected to cross Van-Allen belt 44 times. Moreover, lander geometry was totally new from previous ISRO missions in terms of spacecraft charging aspects. In this paper, the spacecraft requirements in view of spacecraft charging has been analysed. This paper briefly explains the theoretical analysis which estimates the potential developed due to surface and internal charging. Based on this estimation, changes in spacecraft structure were proposed to implement at the design phase and same had been implemented in spacecraft to achieve a successful mission. The guidelines proposed here are applicable to all future lunar missions which passes through multiple orbital maneuver to achieve earth escape velocity and have same kind of structure.

articleTitle: Investigating the Use of Frequency-Modulated Disturbance Injection in Electromagnetic Immunity Testing of Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the use of frequency modulated signals for immunity testing of integrated circuits. The aim is to predict their electromagnetic susceptibility based on realistic noise signals. These signals reflect the complexity and diversity of real electromagnetic disturbances. The approach uses both narrowband and broadband modulation signals during testing as an efficient alternative to the conventional approach using continuous wave signals. The advantages of using the presented interference signals compared to the conventional ones are analyzed and the influence on electromagnetic immunity is shown in comparison using the direct power injection method on an automotive smart power high-side switch.

articleTitle: Radiated Emission Characterization of LED, CFL & Incandescent Bulbs
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Bulbs are the most commonly used items for lighting purposes both domestically and commercially. The most common choice is LED, CFL and Incandescent bulbs. This paper gives a comparative study of Radiated Emission Characterization of the all the three kind of bulbs. Radiated Emission Test were performed on these three bulbs with almost equal power ratings. The test was performed as per MIL STD 461 F. This paper presents the comparative test results of the level of radiated emissions. In the conclusion a brief discussion is given based on the level of emissions which type of bulbs can be suitably used for which applications. The test was performed inside a RF Shielded Semi Anechoic Chamber Located at EMI/EMC facility of Defence Electronics Applications Laboratory (DEAL), Dehradun.

articleTitle: Research on Influence of HV-AN Shielding Box to Radiated Emission According to CISPR 25
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Electromagnetic interference of high-voltage components of electric vehicles play an important role in vehicle electromagnetic compatibility regulatory testing, and engineers pay more attention to design verification test than ever. Since high-voltage artificial network (HV-AN) are used according to CISPR 25, concerns about influence of HV-AN shielding box arise, especially for radiated emission test., Firstly influence of HV-AN shielding box to site validation measurement was analyzed by modeling and simulation, using Modelled Long-wire Antenna Method, and then experimental verifications were carried out. Results show that although amplitude deviation exists in some frequency bands with antenna in horizontal or vertical polarization, little impact on final judgement will occur when shielding box is on table. Subsequently, test layout of site validation with shielding box and HV component radiated emission test was compared. Finally, it is concluded that influence of shielding box to radiated emission test can be ignored under the condition that groundings meet the standard requirement.

articleTitle: Prediction of Conducted Emissions from Various DC-DC Converters by Using Two-Port Noise-Source Equivalent-Circuit Model
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: To predict conducted emissions from a DC-DC converter, we previously proposed a two-port (input and output ports) noise-source equivalent-circuit model, a black-box model, that focuses only on the behavior of the conducted emissions in differential mode. While developing the model, a Si-MOSFET buck converter was used for model validation. The advantage of a black-box model is that it can be easily applied to various types of converters. In this study, we verified our model by applying it to a Si-MOSFET boost converter and GaN-HEMT buck converter. The important features of our model for measurement-based parameter identification are enabling high signal-to-noise ratio measurement on the basis of the waveform-decomposition method we previously proposed and noise-level reduction at higher frequencies due to switching fluctuation. We found that the spectra predicted using our model are in good agreement with the measured spectra with switching fluctuation in terms of both the input and output ports independently of the converter type.

articleTitle: Off-Band Harmonics Mitigation Techniques to Reduce Radiated EMI for a Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Off-band harmonics leading to increased interference problems and performance degradation among radiating elements in a system or with other systems in an electromagnetic polluted environment must be reduced. Here, the response of a printed dipole antenna is determined in terms of its input impedance, reflection coefficient, gain, and radiation pattern. The dipole antenna is designed on a 30 mil RT Duroid substrate and simulations are carried out using CST Microwave Studio.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband SSL-FSS with Band Reject and Flexible Characteristics for Radome Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: This work aims to synthesize a Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) with Band-reject characteristics over an ultra wideband operating range. A Swastika-Square-Loop (SSL) based FSS unit cell was designed to block the WiFi-6E, X and Ku-Bands. The designed conformal periodic structure provides band reject operation over a bandwidth of 12.78 GHz in the intended frequency range. The study of various bends conditions and the change in performance characteristics was studied and a regression based statistical analysis was carried out to establish a relationship between performance characteristics and bend radius. This proposed prediction model would enable the ready use of SSL-FSS based radome for various conformal applications like military equipment or Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV).

articleTitle: Prediction of Radiated ESD fields in a typical Navigation Spacecraft
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: In space, Spacecraft surfaces are charged to several volts due to interaction with space plasma. The potential difference in spacecraft surfaces can cause electrostatic discharges and can radiate electromagnetic field. The fields expected on the subsystems are estimated and assessed the subsystems performance based on radiate susceptibility test results. The amount of radiated field estimated in a particular navigation spacecraft and its effect on spacecraft subsystems are discussed in this paper

articleTitle: EMI Analysis of via stub resonance in a Multi-layer PCB design
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: As the speed and volume of digital data transmission increases, the need to minimize the overall insertion loss in printed circuit boards becomes more important. The design of the via structure in modern circuit boards has a significant impact on the insertion loss, in addition to the transmission line itself. One approach to optimize the via is to reduce the length of the stubs. Long stubs can result in reflections and potentially add fractional wavelength antennas to the circuit, negatively affecting the signal. This paper aims to investigate the impact of via stub resonance and determine ways to avoid the related issues. By routing high-speed signals on layers with shorter via stubs, the effects of remaining stub lengths are studied and the insertion loss profile and FFS are evaluated. The study reveals that the resonance frequency of the via stub has a significant effect on the insertion loss of the signal and hence intends to the EMI problems.

articleTitle: Analysis of Capacitor non-idealities on PDN performance
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Accurate modelling of power distribution network (PDN) design in high-speed systems is a critical challenge. The equivalent electrical circuit of decoupling capacitor (decaps) becomes ambiguous due to temperature, bias voltage and aging dependency. This paper presents a workflow to model the decaps by considering of the temperature and bias voltage as the uncertainty parameters for predicting the PDN impedance. A pareto-front analysis is performed to quantify the uncertain parameter sensitivities on the PDN impedance. A test PDN structure with multiple decaps were analyzed to quantify the variations in the impedance compared to the nominal case. Results show that variations in decap parameters can lead to a 25% overestimation in the overall PDN impedance.

articleTitle: A Study of Signal Integrity on Hybrid Land Grid Array Socket Connector
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: In this paper, the signal integrity(SI) performance on hybrid land grid array(HLGA) socket connector are studied. An innovative force mechanical solution is designed to test SI performance of HLGA socket under different terminal compression. Test results show that when the compression increases relative to the free state, the insertion loss(IL) will be smaller, and the resonance of IL and crosstalk will move to a higher frequency. Multi-physics simulation can well capture the SI performance variation versus mechanical and structural adjustments. Such findings provide a guideline to high-speed socket connector design and evaluation.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Characterization and Mapping of Electrical Properties for Geo Materials at Radio Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: This paper presents the various methods involved in extracting the electrical properties for Geo materials at radio frequencies from 10KHz – 500MHz. The radio frequency signal propagation gets affected by the characterization of the materials and their propagating medium. Extraction of frequency dependent complex relative permittivity and conductivity helps to provide complete database for numerical simulations of electromagnetic wave propagation. From the various methods investigated ASTM D4935 and probe method were selected for extracting electrical properties of the soil and parallel plate capacitor method for concrete. The measured data is compared with the reference data using Altair Feko.

articleTitle: Revised EMI/EMC Test Standard for ISRO Spacecraft subsystems
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Subsystem level EMI/EMC testing is carried out as per tailored version of MIL-STD 461C, which is further modified to develop new EMI/EMC standard for ISRO spacecraft subsystems. The test requirements and test setups are defined such that it will simulate the actual spacecraft conditions. Limit lines are derived for Subsystem level EMI/EMC testing in order to establish the electromagnetic compatibility at spacecraft level. The technical justification for the proposed tests are covered in this paper.

articleTitle: Impact of Discontinuity in the Ground on the Signal Integrity of 100G PAM4 Ethernet
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: In high-speed SerDes, the ground return current plays a critical role in the signal transmission and can negatively affect the signal quality and stability of the system. Discontinuity in the ground will result in an impedance mismatch between the ground planes of different components or subsystems, leading to increased noise, crosstalk, and reflections that significantly degrade the performance of high-speed SerDes. To address this issue, presented is the importance of a well-defined return current path in 100G PAM4 Ethernet through the modeling of package along with board using a 3D Electromagnetic simulation tool. The results provide insight into the effects of resonance and crosstalk, helping designers to avoid mistakes in their designs. Overall, this work is an attempt to provide design engineers with a better understanding of the importance of ground in high-speed SerDes and the steps that need to be taken to ensure reliable and high-performance operation. By incorporating design rules pertaining to ground in the layout, engineers can ensure that their designs are robust and meet the specification for high-speed electrical standards.

articleTitle: Mitigation of EMI in High-Speed PCB designs with Dynamic Phase control
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: In general, well-balanced differential signals radiate less compared to single-ended signals. However, if the two complementary signals of a differential pair are not perfectly balanced, differential pairs often radiate more in the common mode than in the differential mode. In this paper, the mitigation of far-field EMI radiation using dynamic phase control of an unbalanced differential pair is analyzed with an actual design case.

articleTitle: Four-Port SOLR Calibration Algorithm for Symmetric GSSG Probes
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: This paper proposes an efficient four-port short-open-load-reciprocity (SOLR) calibration algorithm for the symmetric Ground-Signal-Signal-Ground (GSSG) probes used for on-wafer S-parameter testing. This algorithm only needs four measurements, including one reciprocal Thru and three traditional calibration standards including Open, Short, and Load. Additionally, the exact S-parameters of the Thru are not mandatorily required. The correctness and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is validated and corroborated by full-wave simulations up to 100 GHz.

articleTitle: ESD Tolerance Improvement of Power Module using Clamp Diodes Built into Control IC
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Higher tolerance to electrostatic discharge (ESD) is desired for protection of equipment for HVAC in electrified transportation applications such as an EV bus. In recent years, Intelligent Power Modules (IPMs) that integrate power chips and ICs are generally applied as components in these HVAC inverters. These power modules control large current and high voltage and are implicitly recognized to have high ESD tolerance. However, in an emitter-sense method, which is one of overcurrent detection methods, power chips with emitter-sense are weak against ESD even though the emitter-sense is a part of the power chip. As a general protection method, it is conceivable to attach an RC filter or protection diode externally to increase the tolerance capacity, but there is a disadvantage that the entire system becomes larger. This paper introduces an ESD tolerance improvement without changing the size of the IPM housing and the operation of the circuit by integrating a protection circuit consisting of clamp diodes in the IC.

articleTitle: A Resistive Pattern Based Microwave Absorber
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: This study describes a C-band wideband circuit analogue absorber. The structure is made up of resonators that are printed on a resistive film mounted on a dielectric substrate in a repeating pattern. The substrate and the ground plane are kept apart from one another by an air spacer. By generating an equivalent circuit model and displaying the normalized impedance plot, the absorber operation is described. The co-cross polarised reflection coefficient and the Polarization conversion ratio (PCR) plot are provided so that one may identify whether or not the structure is an absorber. The absorber is independent of an incident EM wave polarization due to the symmetrically designed resonators on the substrate. The proposed design also achieves 45<sup>o</sup> angular stability for TE (transverse electric) as well as for TM (transverse magnetic) polarization.

articleTitle: Procedure for the Selection of Decoupling Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: This paper examines conducted electromagnetic emission of an integrated circuit, combined with a step by step guide for the optimal selection of decoupling capacitors to reduce the emission in certain frequency ranges. The approach addresses the determination of the parasitic inductances of the capacitor and the loop that is formed when the decoupling capacitor is connected next to an integrated circuit on a printed circuit board. On the basis of measurement examples of a demonstrator board prepared for laboratory exercises, it is shown how an efficient selection for the right decoupling capacitor can be found.

articleTitle: Reliable Electromagnetic Compatibility Near-Field Probing Bench Testing of Electronic Parts : Improvement of EMC Prequalification Method When Replacing Electronic Parts
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: In a printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) of an electronic product, several parts have impact to Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC). If any of these parts needs to be replaced, there is risk that the EMC performance of the electronic product will be impacted due to the part replacement. To ensure continued EMC compliance with the replacement electronic part, manufacturers need to perform standard EMC testing. To minimize the need for more standard EMC testing in the EMC laboratory, there needs to be a reliable prequalification testing activity. The proposed research aims to achieve this purpose. A reliable bench testing setup with a new semi-circular fixture was developed to prequalify replacement parts. The new bench testing setup would help lessen the needed standard EMC testing.

articleTitle: Unified EMC Assurance Case to Assure Safe and Effective Medical Devices with regard to Electromagnetic Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: This paper describes using a graphical notation to document why one believes that a medical device is safe and effective despite being subjected to electromagnetic disturbances. The paper discusses how this approach overcomes the drawbacks of a text-based approach as it visually summarises the claims, arguments and pieces of evidence in a clear, explicit, and easy-to-understand manner. The paper proposes an EMC assurance case using the Goal Structuring Notation. The assurance case covers three complimentary sub-cases: the risk, confidence, and compliance case. The total EMC assurance case provides compelling evidence of how effective EMC risk management is used effectively to manage relevant risks by ensuring EM-resilent design and achieving EMC compliance. It also highlights the interconnectedness among the various subcases. Together, they justify how basic safety, essential performance, and intended use of medical devices are sufficiently guaranteed in the presence of electromagnetic disturbances.

articleTitle: Position-Based Optimization of the Electromagnetic Channel Effective Rank for MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: The electromagnetic channel effective rank of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system describes its effective channel number, which directly characterizes the channel performance and is widely used in the communication systems. In this work, the positions of MIMO transmitting array elements are optimized to achieve the maximum of the effective rank. Specifically, a linear array with fixed aperture size is considered as the transmitting antennas of a MIMO system, and isotropic point receivers are used to model the receivers. The electromagnetic channel matrix with the mutual coupling effect can be derived from the method of moments (MoM). Finally, the best position distributions are obtained by genetic algorithm (GA). The results of comparisons and channel analysis are presented to validate the positive changes of the effective channel capacity.

articleTitle: Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton Transmission Lines for EMI Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: A compact spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) transmission line (TL) helps to reduce electromagnetic interference (EMI). This concept is explained and discussed in this paper. The mutual coupling of two closely spaced SSPP lines is reported in terms of S-parameters and E-field distributions. We can observe that by reducing the gap between the SSPP line to be 0.4mm a good isolation of -20dB can be obtained. The performance of each case is compared with that obtained with the microstrip technology. The benefits of using SSPP-based lines are discussed.

articleTitle: BP-NGD Signal Integrity Application for RLC-Cable Parasitic Dispersion Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: A cable RLC-parasitic dispersion reduction by putting bandpass negative group delay (BP-NGD) circuit to use for signal integrity (SI) and EMC application is stressed. The theoretical formulas of uncommon BP-NGD circuit dedicated to SI enhancement versus parasitic parameters are established. The BP-NGD SI application is confirmed by AC results with circuit design under 250-MHz resonance frequency confirming dispersion reduction of magnitudes and group delays from (15 dB, 10 ns) to better than (2 dB, 1.1 ns). The SI improvement is validated by transient results showing input and output signal delay reduction and envelope cross correlation enhancement from 76% to 98%.

articleTitle: Analytical Modeling of Time Interval Error in CMOS Inverters in presence of Supply and Ground Variations
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to estimate the Time Interval Error (TIE) and jitter in CMOS inverters when Power Supply Noise (PSN) and Ground-Bounce Noise (GBN) are present in the circuit. For that, an analytical expression of TIE and jitter are derived based on the input-output relationship of the inverter circuit, considering the effect of noise. Various examples are presented that support the validity of the proposed method. These examples include diverse experiments considering different parameters and different technology nodes. The results obtained from the simulations using a SPICE base simulator are compared with the ones obtained using the analytical modeling. The different technology nodes of United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC) are used here. Also, the measurement results obtained from the experiments using CMOS inverter integrated circuit (IC) are compared with the proposed analytical modeling. The results obtained using the proposed analytical approach are in congruence with those obtained using the SPICE-based simulator as well as from measurements.

articleTitle: Effect of Aperture Polarization on Lightning Electromagnetic Field Enhancement inside Building Structures at Near and Far Striking Distance
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Critical equipment installed in building structures is at exposure risk to a strong electromagnetic field when a lightning strike occurs in its vicinity. In addition to the electromagnetic field profile created by lightning strikes inside structures, the presence of apertures on these structures causes enhancement in the penetrated lightning electromagnetic field. This paper inspects the implications of aperture orientation on the attributes of the penetrated fields inside the building structures, which is not quantified so far. FEKO electromagnetic simulation software is used for modeling and computation, and the structure is considered present at near and far locale to the lightning strike point. The field enhancement is computed due to multiple apertures at parallel and perpendicular polarization to the incident lightning electromagnetic radiation. It is noted that the penetrated electric field distribution profile inside the building is affected by the aperture polarization; at the same time, the magnetic field contour remains unaltered, irrespective of the lightning strike distance.

articleTitle: Predicting Radiated Emissions from an Electrical Drive System
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: A measurement-based SPICE model is proposed to predict radiated emissions from an electrical drive system over a frequency range from 20-300 MHz. The model combines a model for the radiated emissions from the cabling and housings with a model for coupling inside the electrical motor. The electromagnetic properties of the cabling and housings were captured with measured S-parameters. The coupling mechanisms inside the electrical machine were represented using a circuit- element based model. The intent is to provide insight into how coupling mechanisms and placement of structures in the motor affect radiated emissions from the drive system, and to give the designer an opportunity to evaluate the impact of changes to the motor design. The model was able to predict radiated emissions within several decibels of the measurement over the frequency range of interest, to provide insight into strategies for fixing emissions issues, and to provide estimates for the reduction in emissions that could be expected from each fix.

articleTitle: Air Vent with Non-uniform Cross Section for Improved EMI Shielding and Air Flow
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: The efficient cooling of a system while simultaneously shielding against unwanted electromagnetic energy is a crucial design consideration for air-vents on a system chassis. In this paper, the investigation focuses on the use of air vents with non-uniform cross sections to improve the shielding effectiveness (SE) and air resistance performance. Based on the Bernoulli's principle, several cases of air vent with different non-uniform cross section types were modeled, and both simulation data and measurement results show the improvement in EMI shielding effectiveness and pressure drop of air flow.

articleTitle: Noise measurements at different Satellite Interfaces due to Solar Array Switching Strings
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Switching of solar array strings is a well-known source of electromagnetic emissions on Spacecraft. In order to regulate the bus voltage, the switching strings have Pulse Frequency Modulation (PFM) and Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) to cater to the spacecraft power requirement. High frequency content present in the switching circuitry couples to various interfaces of the spacecraft interfaces that are in close proximity. During disassembled mode testing phase of some of the high power satellites, certain circuits nearby had deviation from nominal performance. To understand the amount of noise coupled to the interfaces, practical measurements have been carried out for the various configurations of the solar array harness types employed in satellite as well as some of the standard interfaces present. The entire practical setup of the solar array simulators with the harness and the switching circuitry have been placed by employing the hardware used for spacecrafts. The switching strings have three types of harness configurations i.e. first is the live and return bundle separately routed, second is the manual twisting of shielded live and return bundle and third is bundle of Twisted pair shielded cable. Six different types of victims have been identified for measurement. The measurements are described and presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Achieving EMC in Spacecraft with Stringent EMC requirements
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Usually spacecraft subsystems are qualified for EMI-EMC based on MIL-STD or test requirements specific to particular organization. Based on the functional requirements of payloads or other subsystems, limits for conducted and radiated EMC tests have to be derived and subsystems should be tested as per those limits and appropriate mitigation have to be followed to achieve EMC. This paper presents three such spacecraft examples and the methods used to achieve EMC.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Based Reduction of Equivalent Electrical Circuits in Power Electronics Application
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: This paper presents an application of an equivalent electric circuit reduction technique to improve the runtime of transient simulations. The approach is based on efficient adjoint sensitivity analyses of the initial electric circuit. Focus is in particular on electric circuits that contain a manageable number of functional elements, potentially of a non-linear type like semiconductor switches, and a much larger number of linear elements that are manifestation of "parasitic effects" as a result of the actual layout and design of the device. The reduction will retain the interpretability of the circuit elements whereas the complexity of the equivalent electric circuit is dramatically reduced. This has the beneficial side effect of stabilizing the transient simulation.The advantage of the proposed method is demonstrated in the conducted emissions simulation of a prototypical inverter. The accuracy of the model is good enough to predict the conducted emissions up to 30 MHz.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of CS114 Test as per MIL-STD 461D to G Requirements, and Experimental Result Comparison for Different Test Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: MIL-STD 461 undergone several changes based on newer development in electronics of military products to keep pace with developments of defense industry. The changes in Military Standard, MIL-STD 461, have made it compatible with changes in the defence industry which follows the guidelines of US Department of Defence. Many changes kept the pace with the demand of the user, its importance and applicability. This paper emphases on CS114 test purpose, the changes introduced based on requirement and procedures with their analysis, starting from MIL-STD 461 D and reaching up to MIL-STD 461G which is latest update and revised version of MIL-STD 461 in its series of development, and the experimental CS114 test data comparison for different leads/cable configuration.

articleTitle: Conducted noise reduction via modulating trigger in copper vapour laser
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: The distinct method of stabilizing the impedance of discharge plasma in copper vapour laser (CVL) by trigger modulation significantly reduced the conducted noise in the system. The level of conducted noise produced by the laser is directly related to the degree of impedance disparity between the laser and the pulse power supply. The intermittent missing of the high voltage discharge pulse applied across the laser head increases the laser impedance due to enhanced time for charge carrier recombination. Experimental research indicates that by missing 0.2% of the high voltage discharge pulse, the conducted noise at the output of the DC supply in the CVL system is reduced by 5dbµV. The conducted noise from the CVL system operated at 9kHz was measured in three different conditions - 1) Without intermittent pulse missing 2) Intermittent pulse missing after every 5 s and 3) Intermittent pulse missing after every 2.5s. This paper presents that besides improving thermal stability and power coupling, the trigger modulation also reduces the electromagnetic interference (EMI) from the CVL system. The technique of mitigating EMI from a gas discharge load by manipulating the plasma impedance can be implemented in other applications that require a decrease in EMI emanating from high-current and high-voltage gas discharges.

articleTitle: Multiband Microwave Metamaterial Absorber for EMI Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: In this paper, a multiband metamaterial absorber for L, S, C, X, and Ku bands is proposed. The proposed unit cell is designed on a low-cost FR-4 substrate and is easy to fabricate. To examine the absorptivity in the multiple frequency bands, the multiband and compact structure is studied and reported. The proposed metamaterial absorber has absorption bands with center frequencies of 1.49 GHz, 2.83 GHz, 3.28 GHz, 4.85 GHz 11.81 GHz, and 13.31 GHz with simulated peak absorptivity of 95, 95, 98, 99, 99, and 99 % respectively.

articleTitle: Propagation of Electrial Fast Transient (EFT) in Radiation mode and its impacts on Equipment under Test
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the propagation of the Electrical fast transient in Radiation mode (air mode) while the testing is done in conducted mode (wire mode) and its effects on the Equipment under Test. This paper gives solutions to protect the equipment under test immune from this noise in Radiated mode (air medium) since the test is done in conducted mode (wire Medium) and the product desingner unaware of the radiated noise coupling while taking protection against Equipment under Test.

articleTitle: Advanced Statistical Methodology to Analyse EMI/EMC Test Data for Inter-laboratory Comparison
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: EMI/EMC testing is a critical step in the design and manufacturing processes of electronic devices. Current methodology used across industry, to select the EMI/EMC test lab is to carry out measurements at various laboratories with similar test method using a source and then do inter-laboratory comparison of the z-score, in accordance with CISPR 32 and ISO/IEC 17025 requirements. The lab with acceptable z-score is selected for the EMI/EMC testing.An advanced statistical methodology backed up by accurate & logical statistical method is proposed in the paper to analyze conducted emission data for Inter-Laboratory Comparison (ILC). To demonstrate the methodology, CE test data for an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) in peak and average detection modes is collected for seven laboratories over the 150 kHz–30 MHz range and advanced analysis is performed. This paper aims to propose further analysis techniques which can provide accurate prediction on various aspects like robust correlation, anomalies on data on few frequencies & arrive at the laboratories which are closer to the laboratory originating the Inter-lab comparison.

articleTitle: Analysis and Modeling Framework of Common Mode Noise in a Three-phase Motor System
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) issue is one of the major constraints of power electronic converters, especially for variable-speed systems. In this work, the common mode noise in a three-phase motor system is analyzed and modeled. The three-phase pulse-width modulation (PWM) inverter creates high magnitudes of dv/dt and di/dt, resulting in common mode noise and disturbance power. In this paper, the common mode noise and disturbance power modeling method are proposed for three-phase motor systems. The proposed equivalent circuit model comprises detailed models for insulated gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs), EMI filters, a three-phase motor and a printed circuit board (PCB). The proposed model of a three-phase system was verified by measurement with and without additional Y-capacitors. The measured and modeled common-mode noise shows a correlation in broadband common-mode noise reduction.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Environment in a Stationary Ship
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Modern naval ships contain large number of RF transmitters and receivers operating at different frequency bands in close proximity due to limited space availability. Most of the antennas used for transmission and reception encounter electromagnetic scatterer in their near field. The switching devices used above-deck use pollutes the naval electromagnetic (EM) environment. The situation aggravates with the increasing demand of transmitter with higher power and receiver with superior sensitivity. However, reliable and concurrent operation of several communication gadgets in naval operation are essential. This obviously impose challenges to the EMC engineers. The objective of the present study is the electromagnetic field strength survey in a stationary naval ship deployed for coast guard patrolling. In this manuscript we presents the measurement results from an comprehensive electromagnetic field survey in a naval ship. Supporting measurement results are also presented.

articleTitle: Indium Tin Oxide based Optically Transparent Wide Band Flexible Circuit Analog Absorber for Optical Window Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: In this paper, a thin, flexible, optically transparent two-layer polarization-insensitive angularly stable broad band circuit analog absorber with octagonal patches of Indium-tin-oxide resistive film patterns on a transparent Polymethyl methacrylate substrate backed by a conducting Indium-tin-oxide ground plane is designed. The structure offers -10 dB reflection bandwidth from 5.52 to 24.26 GHz frequency range, while promising absorption greater than 99% from 7 to 22 GHz with a thickness of 6.5 mm. Absorber is incidence angularly stable for the incidence angles up to 60° for both TE and TM modes. Bending analysis ensures that the proposed absorber can be used for the curved surfaces and the visual transparency makes the structure suitable for see through windows. The design guarantees a fully transparent, low profile, light weight, polarization insensitive angularly stable broadband absorber.

articleTitle: Demystifying the Influence of Channel Components on Signal Integrity (SI) Margin
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Huge demand for functionality, performance and bandwidth has increased the complexity of high-speed designs. Different channel components like central processing unit (CPU) package, add-in-card (AIC) package, printed circuit board (PCB) trace or transmission line, via, and connector parasitics impact eye margins differently. In this paper, peripheral component interconnect express (PCIe) interface is used to demonstrate the same. While PCIe Gen 5 loss budget is 36 dB at 16 GHz Nyquist, depending on these channel components, a design can go above or below this loss requirement. Sensitivity analysis of variations in CPU package, AIC package, PCB transmission lines, and connector in a high-speed channel is studied along with its impact on the overall channel margin.

articleTitle: EMI Control of GDDR6 Design with Drive strength control and On-Die Termination Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 Joint Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (APEMC/INCEMIC)
abstract: Electronic systems are growing extremely dense and coupled in industrial, automotive, and personal computing applications and hence reducing EMI effects become a crucial system design factor Traditional methods of EMI reduction are no longer effective enough to meet regulatory norms and manufacturing demands as technology improvements grow even more sophisticated and applications become more simplified. Conventional EMI reduction methods include using large, expensive filters or reducing switching slew rates, a technique that directly impacts efficiency and the most frequently used shielding techniques that are highly cost effective and at any point can easily lead to catastrophic failure. To realize all the system efficiency along with cost efficient techniques, it is paramount for EMI reduction techniques to resolve the traditional trade-offs which requires creative solutions for both low and high-frequency EMI. This paper talks about a cost-effective EMI reduction technique with the help of an assessment which includes driver support different PU/PD and ODT combinations for the analysis and interpretation of EMC data outcomes defining on a graphic card with their uncertainties.
